 Michael Wilbon taking leave of absence from “PTI” due to health issues
 by 
 Jon Lewis 
 19 seconds ago 
 Share 
 Share 
 Share on X (Twitter) 
 Share on Bluesky 
 Share on Threads 
 Share via Email 
 Copy Link 
 0 
 Washington, DC - September 16, 2013 - DC Studios: Tony Kornheiser and Michael Wilbon on the set of Pardon the Interruption
(Photo by Phil Ellsworth / ESPN Images)
 Little more than a week after the show celebrated its 25th anniversary, “Pardon the Interruption” will be without one half of its venerable duo for the foreseeable future. 
 ESPN “Pardon the Interruption” co-host and NBA analyst Michael Wilbon said in a statement Monday that he will have to take an “indefinite leave of absence” from his roles for the network due to “multiple health issues,” which he indicated have been building over the course of years. Wilbon, 67, characterized the situation as a “trip to the injured list” that he hopes will not be “an extended one.”
 It was only two weeks ago that he and co-host Tony Kornheiser celebrated the 25th anniversary of the show with a special episode. He was also celebrated on the “NBA Today” show where he is a regular contributor. But after hosting “PTI” last Monday, Wilbon missed the rest of the week.
 Speaking on “The Tony Kornheiser Show” Monday , Wilbon said he missed last week’s shows because he was “just exhausted — beyond exhausted, lifeless,” and also indicated that he had been hospitalized. Wilbon: “The bill has come due from too many red-eye flights and just the stuff that I have ignored. And when you’re a diabetic person and you ignore some of these things, the bill comes due and it’s a damn more expensive bill than it might be for other people. … You can’t always pay the bill. The bill comes and it overwhelms you.”
 Wilbon previously suffered a heart attack in 2008, but was not out for a substantial period of time. 
 “I have no idea exactly how this part of my journey will end up,” he said in his statement Monday, “The goal is to come out of it feeling much better than I do now and ready to return to sparring with Tony.”
 A former columnist for The Washington Post, Wilbon was a regular sight on ESPN even before “PTI” as a panelist on “The Sports Reporters.” But it was PTI that launched his television career, which at one point even included hosting ABC’s NBA Finals coverage.
 Kornheiser and Wilbon ultimately transformed the industry with the success of “PTI.” It was not so much that they paved the way for sports columnists to be come television personalities — others had gotten there first — but they changed the role from that of occasional commentator to the entertainer at the center of attention, in much the same way that Roger Ebert and Gene Siskel did for film critics.
 Even as the network’s attention has been focused on Stephen A. Smith’ s “First Take” and “The Pat McAfee Show,” “PTI” has remained the most-watched daily talk show on ESPN, and by a comfortable margin.

 Sports Ratings Tracker SuperMotocross The SMX World Championship Series, including the indoor AMA Supercross Championship and outdoor Pro Motocross Championship, averaged 614,000 viewers on NBC across a Nielsen-measured linear audience and streaming viewership tracked by Adobe Analytics — up 17% from last year. Nielsen updates NBC NFL viewership Nielsen has reprocessed the viewership for NBC’s four NFL games from Week 1-3 of the season. The Patriots-Seahawks Kickoff Game has been updated to 25.2 million, up from an originally-reported 25.1 million. The Week 1 Cowboys-Giants “Sunday Night Football” game has been updated to 25.82 million, up from 25.66 million. Colts-Chiefs the following week has been updated to 24.43 million, up from 24.29 million. Finally, Rams-Broncos in Week 3 has been updated to 20.96 million, up from 20.77 million. WNBA Semis Last Wednesday’s Liberty-Dream WNBA semifinal Game 2 averaged 1.4 million viewers on ESPN, down from Mercury-Lynx in the comparable window last year (1.5M). Last year’s games took place earlier in the calendar and did not face the MLB Postseason. Read more ALDS The MLB American League Division Series was averaging 3.4 million viewers on TNT Sports through Thursday, up 2% from last year’s ALDS on Fox Sports. Last Thursday’s Guardians-White Sox Game 4 averaged 3.8 million opposite NFL “Thursday Night Football,” on par with Brewers-Cubs in the same window last year. Read more Presidents Cup Final round coverage of golf’s Presidents Cup averaged 2.0 million viewers on NBC last Sunday across a Nielsen-measured linear audience (1.1 rating, 1.88M viewers) and streaming viewership tracked by Adobe Analytics — up 37% from the previous edition two years ago and the highest since 2017 (four telecasts). NASCAR “Big Data” NASCAR last week resumed reporting the official Nielsen “Big Data + Panel” ratings and viewership figures for its races, a move that coincides with Nielsen having rolled out a modified version of the methodology at the end of last month. The first race following that decision, Darlington over Labor Day weekend, averaged a 1.0 rating and 1.98 million viewers on USA Network — up 6% and 5% respectively from last year (1.0, 1.9M). Read more Daytona NASCAR Cup Series racing from Daytona averaged a 1.7 rating and 3.12 million viewers on NBC a week ago Saturday, per the “Big Data + Panel” methodology that is the official Nielsen currency, and a 1.8 and 3.51 million under the old “panel-only” metric NASCAR now publicizes for its races.
